answers.reason: The student holds no office and does not decide university-wide statutes and strategy.
The student has no role in central budget allocation.
The student is not involved in hiring professors.
The student holds no office, whereas the elected student representative speaks for students in formal faculty governance.
The student holds no representative office to advise the faculty council on degree programmes.
The examination board decides on the cases of individual students rather than being a participatory body for regular students without office.
The student is enrolled in a bachelor programme and does not conduct faculty research projects.
Rewriting module descriptions is a task for teaching staff and programme officials, not an unappointed student.
The student has no responsibility for purchasing laboratory equipment.
Every member has one place where their matters are decided, and orientation week planning is the most fitting occasion for a regular student without office.
